title: Law firm business development: a patent litigation playbook
summary: Build a practice-led law firm business development system for patent litigation: choose priorities, qualify signals, and follow through.
body_markdown:
Law firm business development is the disciplined work of turning client insight, credible experience, and relationships into an appropriate next step. Marketing helps a firm become visible and understood. Business development, or BD, helps the right people act on a real client need. The focus here is firm growth and client development, not BD careers or job descriptions. For patent-litigation teams, a filing, referral, or client conversation begins a decision process. It never authorizes an automatic pitch. This U.S.-focused operating model is practical guidance, not legal advice or a substitute for firm-specific ethics and conflicts review.


## Key takeaways


- Business development is a shared client-service system. It connects a priority and a verified need to a useful response with an owner and review date.
- A patent-litigation signal requires relationship context, relevant experience, conflicts and capacity procedures, information controls, and local ethics review before outreach.
- Lawyers own trust and judgment. BD staff make the intelligence, coordination, and follow-through reliable enough to repeat.


## What law firm business development is


Law firm business development is the practice of winning, retaining, and appropriately expanding the right client relationships by connecting a verified need to a credible, coordinated response. It covers priority selection, relationship development, client feedback, pursuit decisions, referrals, service expansion, and learning from outcomes.


Marketing and BD share the goal of sustainable firm growth, and their boundaries vary by firm. Their immediate jobs differ. A QorusDocs guide hosted by[Thomson Reuters](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en-us/posts/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2023/01/BizDev-Legal-Guide-TR-MPF.pdf) describes marketing as communicating the firm's value to a target audience and BD as identifying and acting on strategic growth opportunities.


Marketing usually emphasizes Business development usually emphasizes


Positioning, reputation, visibility, and market messages Priority relationships, verified needs, pursuit decisions, and follow-through


Websites, thought leadership, public relations, events, and campaigns Client teams, relationship plans, referrals, qualified opportunities, and feedback


Reach, engagement, and awareness Appropriate next actions, matter outcomes, client retention, and learning


A webinar, partner lunch, alert, or conference can create useful context. None is a result by itself. The meaningful unit of BD work is a client-relevant next action with a responsible owner and a date for review.


## Set the professional-conduct and information perimeter first


An apparently relevant matter, relationship, or filing does not clear a contact, create a client relationship, resolve a conflict, or permit use of information in an outreach. The applicable state rules, court rules, admission status, recipient location, and communication medium all matter. The American Bar Association Model Rules provide a baseline, while individual jurisdictions control.


- **Keep every communication accurate and supported.** ABA[Model Rule 7.1](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_7_1_communication_concerning_a_lawyer_s_services/) bars false or misleading communications about a lawyer or the lawyer's services. Claims about results, rankings, experience, client logos, testimonials, comparisons, or specialization need substantiation, permission, and local review. A disclaimer cannot cure a materially misleading impression. Model Rule 7.2 also places conditions on[referrals and specialist claims](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_7_2_advertising/) .
- **Control solicitation and referral activity.** Prospect-specific live outreach, lead sources, reciprocal arrangements, compensation, and opt-outs are jurisdiction- and medium-specific. ABA[Model Rule 7.3](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_7_3_direct_contact_with_prospective_clients/) defines solicitation and prohibits contact involving coercion, duress, or harassment. It also requires lawyers to stop when a recipient has expressed a desire not to be solicited. A sophisticated corporate recipient does not provide blanket approval for a campaign.
- **Separate approved experience from confidential matter material.** Use only approved descriptions, roles, names, logos, pricing, results, and work product. ABA[Model Rule 1.6](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_1_6_confidentiality_of_information/) covers information relating to a representation and requires reasonable efforts against unauthorized disclosure or access. A useful experience record is permission-aware. It is never a raw copy of the matter file.
- **Limit prospective-client intake and run conflicts procedures.** Collect only the information needed for the firm's controlled fit and conflicts decision before a detailed exchange. Model Rule 1.18 protects information learned from a[prospective client](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_1_18_duties_of_prospective_client/) , even when no relationship follows. Current-client conflicts remain governed by[Model Rule 1.7](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_1_7_conflict_of_interest_current_clients/) .
- **Supervise staff, agencies, and tools.** Under[Model Rule 5.3](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_5_3_responsibilities_regarding_nonlawyer_assistant/) , partners and lawyers with comparable managerial authority must make reasonable efforts to ensure the firm maintains measures that give reasonable assurance that associated nonlawyers act compatibly with lawyers' professional obligations. Lawyers with direct supervisory authority must make reasonable efforts to ensure that the supervised nonlawyer's conduct is compatible with those obligations. ABA Formal Opinion 501 explains that the controlling jurisdiction may differ and addresses lawyer responsibility for[solicitation by others](https://www.americanbar.org/content/dam/aba/administrative/professional_responsibility/ethics-opinions/aba-formal-opinion-501.pdf) . A vendor's signal is an input. Attorneys decide fit, contact permissibility, supporting evidence, and final wording.


Patent practice adds a boundary. The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) rules in[37 C.F.R. § 11.701](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-37/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-11/subpart-D/section-11.701) ,[§ 11.702](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-37/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-11/subpart-D/section-11.702) , and[§ 11.703](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-37/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-11/subpart-D/section-11.703) address communications and solicitation by practitioners before the Office. They are not a universal rulebook for patent litigation. State and court rules will often govern litigation conduct, so a firm should obtain local ethics review for a specific campaign.


**Before case-triggered outreach, confirm the local advertising and solicitation rules, conflicts process, information permissions, relationship context, and partner approval.**


## Choose where the practice intends to grow


Your first operating decision is focus. Select a limited portfolio of priority clients, prospects, sectors, and referral relationships. The right size depends on the firm's resources and the depth of work required, so a universal account count creates false precision.


Assess each possible priority against:


- strategic and long-term fit;
- relationship depth and access;
- demonstrated service quality and approved experience;
- technology, industry, venue, and procedural fit;
- a confirmed or plausible client need;
- conflicts, capacity, and resource constraints; and
- value to the client and the practice over time.


Each chosen priority should have a partner owner, a BD lead, a concise client-value hypothesis, a relationship map, one agreed next action and date, and a review cadence. These are management facts, not sales collateral.


Client expansion should begin with service. A practice asks what the client is trying to achieve, where the firm has relevant evidence and judgment, and whether an introduction would help. Fairfax Associates' practitioner guidance warns that client programs lose credibility when the perceived purpose is simply to increase client spending. Its[client-program analysis](https://fairfaxassociates.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/12/BuildingBetterClientPrograms.pdf) instead starts with value from the client's perspective, clear relationship-partner accountability, and selective focus.


For a patent-litigation group, focus may mean a technical sector in which the team has verified experience, an existing client with an emerging need, or a referral relationship where both sides understand the value. High filing volume alone is a weak reason to designate a market as a priority.


## Build evidence and relationship context before the signal


Your team should be able to answer three questions before reacting to an alert: Why us? Why now? Who should lead the conversation?


Maintain a living relationship-and-matter intelligence layer for each priority. It should identify relevant stakeholders, relationship strength, known client strategy, service feedback, approved experience, relevant practices, panel or competing-firm context where legitimately known, the owner, the next action, and the review date.


Useful experience evidence is narrower than a matter database. A lawyer-validated record can include the permitted matter description, the firm's role, the industry or technology, the issue or procedure, venue, team, and result when disclosure is allowed. It should also record permission limits and a review or expiry date. A Legal Marketing Association (LMA) case study about Orrick describes how properly tagged experience records can be mapped against client and market insight to identify[differentiators and gaps](https://connect.legalmarketing.org/browse/blogs/blogviewer?BlogKey=6b901129-ee6f-46d7-a902-41b510f1878c) .


For patent litigation, public signals may include technical or market changes, portfolio and standards activity, licensing or transaction context, litigation patterns, venue developments, panel changes, referrals, and new filings. Keep privileged analysis, protected documents, and unapproved client facts outside the BD record and outside third-party tools.


Any early assessment should remain proportionate and source-grounded. A complaint records allegations. It does not establish infringement, validity, conflict clearance, or any other legal conclusion.


## Turn a patent-litigation signal into a qualified opportunity


A new patent case can be a market signal. It becomes a qualified opportunity only after the team considers relationship context, strategic fit, credible experience, firm procedures, capacity, and whether it has a useful reason to contact the prospective client or referral source. The first question is: Would an informed response be helpful, permissible, and owned?


The operating sequence is short:


1. **Capture the signal and context.** A client conversation, referral, public filing, or market event surfaces a possible need. Record the source and connect it to an existing priority or explain why it deserves an exception.
2. **Name the owners and triage.** A partner and BD lead consider relationship context and strategic fit. They follow the firm's conflicts, confidentiality, capacity, and local ethics procedures before outreach.
3. **Qualify the opportunity.** Define the client-relevant problem, comparable approved experience, relationship path, commercial basis, and reasonable next action. Close, recycle, or decline a signal that lacks a sound reason to proceed.
4. **Make a useful response.** Offer relevant insight, a coordinated introduction, or a proportionate source-grounded assessment when appropriate. A generic credentials deck should not lead the conversation.
5. **Record and learn.** Capture the owner, next step and date, stage, and eventual reason for a win, loss, decline, or no-go. Feed the result back into priorities, experience evidence, and relationship plans.


Legal analytics practitioners have described alerts as a common starting point for Am Law litigation BD. They also describe the client problem created by an immediate flood of generic pitches. The practical lesson from the ABA's[client-research discussion](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/law_practice/resources/law-technology-today/2024/how-attorneys-are-shoring-up-client-research-for-the-perfect-pitch/) is to demonstrate client value and understand the client's world instead of reciting credentials.


“Qualified” is an internal operating label. It is not ethical clearance, conflict clearance, or a prediction of work. Firms should define stages in plain language and avoid universal scores, preset thresholds, or arbitrary outreach deadlines.

Lawyers still decide fit, follow the firm's conflicts and ethics procedures, review the evidence, approve the work product, and control the final communication.

## Make the response useful, then run the client team


A useful response demonstrates understanding of the client's situation. Speed has limited value when the message is generic, unsupported, or sent through the wrong relationship path.


Bring together the relationship partner, the relevant patent-litigation lawyers, and the BD or client-development lead. They should agree on the apparent client need, the evidence the firm may responsibly use, the relationship handoff, and one next action. Ask who should speak, what the client already knows, what the firm can add, and what information should remain outside the pursuit record.


The team may decide that a technical issue warrants reviewable, source-grounded work product before a conversation. Depending on the need, that could mean work to[build a defensible evidence-of-use record](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/ai-patent-infringement-detection) , prepare[trial-ready invalidity and evidence-of-use claim charts](https://www.tryandai.com/product/claim-charts) for attorney review, or[test the prior art position](https://www.tryandai.com/product/prior-art-search) . These are optional evidence paths. None is a required step in every pursuit, and no early assessment should be presented as a final legal conclusion.


A qualified opportunity may advance into the firm's normal proposal or request-for-proposal process only after its usual qualification and conflicts procedures. Keep that pursuit controlled. Align the relationship owner, substantive team, BD lead, and evidence before the firm commits resources or sends a response. The proposal process itself is a separate body of work.


After contact, the client team should record the response and next action while respecting information permissions. Silence, a decline, or a request to stop is an outcome to honor and learn from.


## Make partner judgment and BD operations work together


Lawyers and BD staff have complementary responsibilities. Clear ownership prevents follow-up from disappearing between relationship judgment and operational execution.


Role Owns Does not own alone


Partners and lawyers Client listening and trust, legal and commercial judgment, substantive response, relationship handoffs, conflicts escalation, and final communication Research coordination, data hygiene, pursuit logistics, or staff-led outreach without lawyer direction


BD and client-development staff Account-plan facilitation, approved research, relationship maps, experience-data hygiene, project management, credential development, coaching, reporting, and review cadence Legal or ethical clearance, conflict decisions, legal conclusions, or final client communications


Practice leadership Priority choices, capacity and resources, accountability, origination-credit issues, escalation, and review discipline Day-to-day client judgment on a specific matter


Use a light recurring rhythm: a short monthly partner-led pursuit review, a quarterly priority-account and client-team review, and a debrief after meaningful wins, losses, no-go decisions, and client-feedback moments. ABA practitioner guidance on durable BD emphasizes[alignment and reinforcement](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/law_practice/resources/law-practice-today/2026/february-2026/how-law-firms-build-business-development-that-lasts/) rather than episodic plans that fade after launch.


The test of collaboration is better client service and a clear next step. The number of client relationship management (CRM) entries is an administrative signal, not proof of value. A practice-specific[workflow for patent litigation law firms](https://www.tryandai.com/solutions/law-firms) can support this operating rhythm after the team has defined ownership and judgment boundaries.


## Measure learning before claiming results


Define each measure and its attribution rules before you build a dashboard. Then track both the health of the operating system and outcomes. There is no universal weighting or benchmark for every practice.


**Leading indicators** show whether the work is moving:


- priority-account plans covered and refreshed as agreed;
- meaningful client-feedback interactions and relationship coverage;
- approved experience evidence available for a priority;
- qualified needs with a named owner;
- next actions completed by the agreed date;
- pipeline ageing and stage progression; and
- debriefs completed and findings applied.


**Outcome indicators** show what followed:


- qualified opportunities by account and pursuit type;
- proposal and interview outcomes with stated reasons;
- appropriate new matters;
- client retention or expansion;
- referral conversion and client feedback; and
- revenue, margin, and realization where the firm's attribution method supports the connection.


Activity counts need context. Meetings, contacts, alerts, cross-practice introductions, and CRM records do not prove that the activity caused revenue. Pipeline is a forecast based on assumptions. It is never booked work.


Review patterns by account, signal source, and pursuit type. Legal buying cycles are long and nonlinear, so firmwide totals can hide useful differences. A no-go decision may protect a relationship or scarce capacity. Good service and candid client feedback can improve the system even when no new matter follows. One LMA-published large-firm case study illustrates the value of tracking matters, client feedback, and revenue together while treating them as[distinct measures](https://connect.legalmarketing.org/browse/blogs/blogviewer?BlogKey=b94bc09b-bceb-4e1c-b153-7dbc59dffcc8&hlmlt=BL) .


## Start with a governed pilot


Start with a limited, strategically coherent portfolio and a defined operating rhythm. Add technology after you have set the practice's priorities, permissions, and decision rights.


1. Select the pilot accounts, sectors, or referral relationships using the practice's focus criteria.
2. Name the lawyer and BD owners. Document the local ethics, conflicts, and information-use rules that govern the pilot.
3. Clean only the approved experience and relationship data needed for those priorities.
4. Run a monthly pursuit review and a quarterly client-team review. Include at least two client-feedback or win/loss debriefs during the pilot.
5. Adjust priority choices, response practices, ownership, and measures before expanding the program or adding tools.


This sequence is an implementation pattern, not a universal 90-day formula. The relevant cadence depends on the practice and its buying cycles. A candid client conversation and lawyer judgment remain more valuable than workflow volume.


## Frequently asked questions


### How is business development different from law firm marketing?


Marketing creates awareness and a clear market message; business development turns prioritized relationships and client needs into an owned next step. Marketing often leads positioning, thought leadership, events, public relations, and campaigns. BD often leads account priorities, relationship plans, pursuit decisions, follow-through, and debriefs. The functions overlap by firm and should share client insight.


### What makes patent-litigation business development different?


Patent-litigation BD often depends on a focused record of relevant experience, technical context, relationship access, and careful judgment about a case or another market signal. A complaint or alert may help a team notice a need. It does not establish the merits, clear conflicts, create a relationship, or permit outreach. Lawyers must apply the firm's ethics, information, capacity, and approval procedures before acting.


### What should a law firm measure for business development?


Measure the health of the operating system and appropriately attributed outcomes. Useful operating measures include priority-plan coverage, relationship depth, qualified needs, next-action completion, pipeline ageing, and debrief completion. Outcome measures can include new matters, retention, expansion, referrals, client feedback, and financial results where the attribution method supports them. Activity counts alone do not show causation.


A durable patent-litigation BD practice chooses where to focus, maintains approved evidence and relationship context, qualifies signals under lawyer control, makes a useful response, and learns from the outcome. The system should improve client service even when the right answer is to wait, decline, or stop.
